text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SEVODNYA
- The Russian authorities, expecting to receive a new 'coal loan' from the World Bank, may face a scandal because the previous loan had not been used according to conditions set by World Bank.
- Russia's Defence Minister Igor Rodionov is to visit China on April 14-18 to discuss perspectives of the two countries' military cooperation.
- As talks about the possibility of joining NATO intensify in Kiev, Western military experts are visiting Ukraine more often.
- St Petersburg mayor Vladimir Yakovlev said his city was prepared to issue $300 million in Eurobonds.
- Russia failed to negotiate full liberalisation of steel trade with Western countries at talks with the European Union.
- The parliamentary committee turned down the draft law on the natural resourses which presupposed revising property rights, and backed full state control over natural resourses.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The Chairman of Russia's Supreme Court said criminal structures often implement court rulings instead of bailiffs for a certain fee.
- Though World Bank's attitude to Russia is more positive than that of IMF, there may be some problems with new loans.
- According to an economic liberty rating of 150 countries compiled by experts from The Heritage Foundation and The Wall Street Journal, Russia shares 115-117 places with Albania and Lesotho.

- During the Prime Minister's two days absence, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais approved a new concept to run state property and put on discussion of the state stakes of the country's gas giant Gazprom on the government's agenda.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russia has accelerated activity in Chechnya and appears about ready sign some bilateral agreements with the region.
- Deputy Prime Minister Alfred Kokh criticised the low efficiency of the state-run enterprises and natural monopolies.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- Chechnya is slowly overcoming its political crisis, but economy is not functioning in the region, says Ivan Rybkin, Russia's national security chief, after a visit to Chechnya.
PRAVDA-5
- President Yeltsin who publicly fights against corruption and privileges, created special conditions for his own family.
KOMSOMOLSKAYA PRAVDA
- A car in Russia is not just a means of transport, but a means of political self-expression, says a paper in a comment on the idea make Russian officials use only Russian cars.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
